cohort: The study included 59 obese, normoglycemic pregnant women and 58 non-obese, normoglycemic pregnant controls recruited from an antenatal clinic.
finding: Maternal obesity was associated with 3.21 times higher odds of elevated newborn glycated albumin levels and lower 5-min APGAR scores in offspring compared to non-obese women.
cross-section timing: At delivery, following recruitment at 36 weeks of gestation.
